source.title: Learning before memorising: How far does early stopping protect multilayer perceptrons from label noise?

record.tranche_reason: Tests memorisation and clean-test performance under partial label corruption, plus learning dynamics; it does not use the original completely-random-label experiment.
record.gate_note: The study tests symmetric noise only up to 60%, not an entirely random labeling. Results on corrupted-label memorisation, clean-test accuracy, and learning dynamics bear on the versions. It reports no experiment on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, Gaussian-noise inputs, dropout, or data augmentation.
record.test_reason: Own experiments on a small digits MLP test degradation and memorisation under partial symmetric noise, strong weight decay, and clean-versus-corrupted learning order. This is a new setting; fully random labels and their fitting time are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: noisy-validation early stopping exploits a learning-before-memorising window under symmetric noise, but that window largely closes under pair-flip noise. The authors also conclude that memorisation alone does not determine generalization harm.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a small two-hidden-layer MLP trained with Adam on an 8 × 8 handwritten-digits dataset; tests partial symmetric and structured pair-flip corruption, rather than completely random labels on the original settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise structure changes the outcome: symmetric noise separates learning from memorisation, while pair-flip noise makes them overlap. Noise rate also changes clean test accuracy and memorisation.

fits_no_version.finding: Noisy-validation epoch selection retains high test accuracy under symmetric noise and is less effective under pair-flip noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The effectiveness of noisy-validation early stopping depends on the structure of label corruption.

fits_no_version.finding: The random forest and MLP both reproduce every corrupted label at 40% symmetric noise, but achieve test accuracies of 0.941 and 0.639.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Equal corrupted-label memorisation can coexist with substantially different generalization across classifier families.

record.code_released: available from the corresponding author on reasonable request
record.peer_reviewed: Journal of Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Neural Network, 6(2), 2026
record.problems: Uses one low-dimensional image dataset and small fully connected networks; only five seeds; tests two synthetic noise models, not instance-dependent or real annotation noise. The authors note that pooled paired tests treat noise rates from the same seed as separate pairs.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted detailed clean-test accuracy rows for MLP-L2 and additional comparator models across the noise-rate tables; retained MLP and MLP-ES accuracy, MLP/MLP-ES/MLP-L2 memorisation, RF's memorisation/generalization contrast, and the dynamics results relevant to the claim.

untested.parts: Entirely random labeling, resulting overall training error and chance test performance with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Time to fit true versus entirely random labels and convergence time across corruption fractions. Early-stopping runtime and within-run learning order do not test these.
The full sweep to entirely random labels, chance endpoint, and quantitative confirmation of zero overall training error. Memorisation rates cover only corrupted examples.
Dropout, data augmentation, fully random labels, eventual fitting beyond 500 epochs, and exact removal of all explicit regularization. The nominally unregularised baseline retains alpha = 0.00001.
Fully random labels, larger architectures and datasets, and real annotation noise.

missing.what: 20% symmetric-noise dynamics: 95% clean fit at epoch 9.8 ± 2.2, memorisation then 1.6 ± 0.7%, and 50% memorisation at epoch 98.6 ± 10.3.

record.verdict_notes: No V1 verdict follows merely from omitting fully random labels. V2 is untested, rather than tested but unextracted. Early stopping is outside V5's named interventions. Structured pair-flip dynamics qualify V6, rather than V4's random-noise degradation claim. Strong-weight-decay results concern finite training and partial corruption, not proof that eventual random-label fitting is impossible.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test completely random labeling of the entire training set, or report overall training error under such labeling; tests partial symmetric and pair-flip corruption on one small MLP.

Does not compare time to fit true versus completely random labels or measure convergence time across fractions of random corruption. It reports early-stopping runtime, but that is not the time comparison specified here.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Tests selected partial symmetric and pair-flip corruption rates, not a full sweep from no corruption to completely random labels for every network; does not establish that all variants fit the whole training set perfectly.

Compares an unregularised MLP, weight decay, and early stopping under label noise; does not test dropout or data augmentation, nor whether removing each method by itself harms generalization on true labels.
Measures learning and memorisation under symmetric and pair-flip noise, not fully random labels or the exact Arpit et al. experiment.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope

reader_labels.reason: The unregularised MLP reproduces all corrupted labels under partial symmetric noise, but the study does not test an entirely random labeling of the full training set (R8–R13).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Symmetric noise, unregularised MLP versus early-stopped MLP
reader_labels.reason: The unregularised MLP reproduces corrupted labels completely as noise increases and its clean test accuracy falls; early stopping keeps memorisation low and retains higher test accuracy, so the claim does not describe both variants uniformly (R5–R7, R13, R19, R26–R27).
